description: Backslash escape sequences inside single-quoted string literals, matching Snowflake. A '...' literal accepts BOTH quote doubling ('' becomes ') and BACKSLASH escapes: \' becomes ', \\ becomes a single backslash, and \n / \t / \r become their control characters. A backslash before an OCTAL DIGIT yields that control character, so '\2' is the single character 0x02 and not a backslash followed by a digit - LENGTH proves it is one character. Any OTHER backslash is simply DROPPED, so '\%' is just %. All decode sites share SqlStringLiterals and the lexer treats a backslash as always beginning an escape, so the boundaries agree. The headline case is a stored procedure whose '-quoted body builds dynamic SQL with backslash-escaped quotes, a shape Snowflake exports produce: the body is decoded ONCE at CREATE and re-parsed at CALL, so both layers have to agree - previously the body was left with stray backslashes that failed to re-lex (token recognition error at: '\'). The last test proves the built SQL not only looks clean but actually EXECUTES. Converted 1:1 from scripting/BackslashStringEscapeTest (now retired); the procedure bodies are written on one line here, which changes nothing about the escaping under test.

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE build_stmt("COL" VARCHAR, "VAL" VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS 'BEGIN LET stmt VARCHAR := ''UPDATE t SET '' || :col || '' = \\'''' || :val || ''\\'';''; RETURN stmt; END;'

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE ins_val("V" VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS 'BEGIN LET stmt VARCHAR := ''INSERT INTO tvals VALUES (\\'''' || :v || ''\\'')''; EXECUTE IMMEDIATE stmt; RETURN ''ok''; END;'
